papers.title: Single-cell landscape reveals PLPP2 upregulation underlying radiotherapy resistance and immune microenvironment remodeling in pancreatic cancer.
papers.abstract: The main purpose of this study was to investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying radiotherapy resistance in pancreatic cancer by integrating single-cell transcriptomic analysis with multicenter clinical cohorts. Using machine learning algorithms and genomic data, we identified key genes associated with radiotherapy response by analyzing radiotherapy sensitivity in our center's single-cell cohort together with external multicenter cohorts, combined with immune microenvironment remodeling and metabolic reprogramming. Radiotherapy resistance- and prognosis-related genes were identified using
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell transcriptomics with multicenter clinical cohorts to identify PLPP2 upregulation as a driver of radiotherapy resistance in pancreatic cancer. The findings link PLPP2 to immune microenvironment remodeling and metabolic reprogramming, suggesting it as a potential biomarker or therapeutic target.

papers.title: A spectral framework for measuring diversity in multiple sequence alignments.
papers.abstract: Machine learning (ML) methods for proteins and RNAs rely on multiple sequence alignments (MSAs) and related datasets such as experimental mutagenesis libraries, yet the amount of usable information they contain remains unclear. Here, a spectral measure of information is recast into an interpretable quantity for MSAs, denoted Leff, defined as the number of fully independent alignment positions that reproduce the observed sequence diversity. Applied to RNA MSAs, this measure shows that evolutionary constraints nearly halve diversity relative to the secondary structure alone, quantifying function
papers.summary: The paper introduces Leff, a spectral measure that quantifies the effective number of independent positions in a multiple sequence alignment by capturing how much sequence diversity is present. Applied to RNA alignments, it reveals that evolutionary constraints reduce diversity by nearly half compared to what secondary structure alone would predict, providing a way to quantify functional information in MSAs.

papers.title: An atlas of colonization factors in the mouse gut microbiome reveals phylogenetically structured repertoires and infection-stage-associated variation during Toxoplasma gondii infection in mice.
papers.abstract: Colonization factors (CFs) comprise CF-associated gene families related to microbial establishment, persistence, host interaction, and gut ecological fitness, but their organization and variation in the mouse gut microbiome remain poorly defined. We integrated the Mouse Gut Genome Catalogue and the Mouse Gut Protein Catalogue, clustered at 90% amino acid identity, to define CF repertoires. A total of 79 conserved CF families, comprising over 2.4 million homologs, were identified across 112,951 genomes from 2,824 microbial species. Species-level CF-associated gene profiles exhibited a clear phy
papers.summary: This study built a comprehensive atlas of colonization factors (CFs) across the mouse gut microbiome by integrating two large catalogues, identifying 79 conserved CF families with over 2.4 million homologs spanning 112,951 genomes and 2,824 species. The authors found that CF repertoires are phylogenetically structured and that their abundance varies with infection stage during Toxoplasma gondii infection in mice. This provides a resource for understanding how gut microbes establish and persist, and how infection reshapes these colonization-associated gene families.

papers.title: Deep genomic models of allele-specific measurements.
papers.abstract: Allele-specific quantification of sequencing data allows for a systematic investigation of how DNA sequence variations influence cis gene regulation. Current methods for analyzing allele-specific measurements for causal analysis rely on statistical associations between genetic variation across individuals and allelic imbalance. Instead, we propose DeepAllele, a novel deep learning sequence-to-function model using paired allele-specific input, designed to learn sequence features that predict subtle changes in gene regulation between alleles. Our approach is suited for datasets with unambiguous
papers.summary: DeepAllele is a deep learning sequence-to-function model that uses paired allele-specific measurements to learn DNA sequence features predicting subtle allele-specific changes in gene regulation. Unlike traditional population-level association methods, it directly models cis-regulatory effects from allele pairs, enabling causal analysis of how sequence variants influence regulation.

papers.title: Identification of immune cell mitochondrial dysfunction characteristics and clinical predictive biomarkers in sepsis via multi-cohort machine learning and single-cell RNA sequencing.
papers.abstract: Sepsis involves dysregulated host responses with mitochondrial dysfunction as a key mechanism, yet its immune cell landscape and clinical utility are unclear.
papers.journal: Inflammation research : official journal of the European Histamine Research Society ... [et al.]
papers.summary: This study investigates mitochondrial dysfunction in immune cells during sepsis using multi-cohort machine learning and single-cell RNA sequencing. The authors aim to characterize the immune cell landscape and identify clinical predictive biomarkers, addressing a gap in understanding the clinical utility of mitochondrial dysfunction in sepsis.

papers.title: ProtThermoRank: Sequence-based multi-class prediction model for protein thermal stability changes and its application to CcsZ.
papers.abstract: Protein thermal stability is a key property of industrial enzymes and biopharmaceutical proteins. The rapid and accurate evaluation of thermal stability across large numbers of variants has become a critical step in protein engineering. However, experimental screening of large mutational landscapes remains time-consuming, labor-intensive, and costly. Here, we present ProtThermoRank, a sequence-based multiclass prediction model for mutation-induced changes in protein thermal stability. Unlike existing approaches that encode reference and mutant sequences independently, ProtThermoRank explicitly
papers.summary: ProtThermoRank is a sequence-based machine learning model that predicts mutation-induced changes in protein thermal stability as a multi-class problem, rather than encoding reference and mutant sequences independently. The authors demonstrate its utility by applying it to CcsZ, showing it can rapidly evaluate large mutational landscapes that would otherwise require costly experimental screening.

papers.title: Development and validation of a blood-based diagnostic model for pulmonary tuberculosis combining GBP5 expression and routine laboratory indicators.
papers.abstract: WHO reports that only 54% of tuberculosis (TB) patients received rapid diagnostic tests at their initial presentation. Conventional laboratory methods in TB detection have high specificity (>90%) but low sensitivity (<50%). This means a large number of tuberculosis patients are missed. A better diagnostic approach is essential to decrease the TB burden. Studies on multi-indicator blood-based models for rapid TB diagnosis remain limited. We developed a rapid, non-sputum-based model to improve the efficiency of TB diagnosis. This was a retrospective case-control study including 301 patients with
papers.summary: This retrospective case-control study developed and validated a blood-based diagnostic model for pulmonary tuberculosis that combines GBP5 gene expression with routine laboratory indicators. The goal is to improve on conventional TB tests, which have high specificity but low sensitivity and miss many patients. The multi-indicator model aims to provide a rapid, non-sputum-based diagnostic approach.

papers.title: Integrated multi-omics and experimental analyses reveal VIPR1 as a potential mediator linking environmental bisphenol A exposure to MASH-HCC progression.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis-related liver cancer (MASH-HCC) is an increasingly important subtype of hepatocellular carcinoma, and environmental contaminants have been proposed as potential contributors to its progression. Bisphenol A (BPA), a ubiquitous endocrine-disrupting chemical, has been implicated in metabolic dysfunction and liver injury. However, the molecular mechanisms linking BPA exposure to MASH-HCC remain incompletely understood. In this study, we employed an integrated framework combining transcriptomic analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis,
papers.summary: This study integrates transcriptomic data with network analysis and experimental validation to identify VIPR1 as a potential molecular mediator connecting bisphenol A (BPA) exposure to the progression of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis-related liver cancer (MASH-HCC). The findings suggest that environmental BPA exposure may promote liver cancer progression through VIPR1-related pathways, highlighting a gene-environment interaction in this HCC subtype.

papers.title: Developing SCL2205: A Protein Sequence-based Spatial Modelling Dataset for the Protein Language Model Frontier.
papers.abstract: Deep learning (DL) has substantially advanced protein subcellular localisation (SCL) prediction, yet its potential remains constrained by suboptimal input preparation and limited high-quality reference data. Furthermore, existing state-of-the-art (SoTA) predictors suffer from performance metric inflation due to unmitigated training-to-testing data leakage during homology augmentation. We address these challenges by introducing SCL2205, a leak-minimised benchmark dataset and pipeline curated specifically to support trustworthy, scalable, and reproducible DL-based SCL modelling.
papers.summary: The authors present SCL2205, a new benchmark dataset and pipeline for predicting protein subcellular localisation that minimises data leakage between training and test sets. They show that existing state-of-the-art predictors suffer from inflated performance metrics due to homology-based leakage, and their leak-minimised resource aims to enable more trustworthy and reproducible deep learning models.

papers.title: VirPLM: Antigenic prediction of influenza A/H3N2 viruses with a fine-tuned protein language model.
papers.abstract: Human influenza A/H3N2 viruses undergo rapid antigenic evolution primarily driven by the hemagglutinin subunit 1 (HA1). Within HA1, amino acid substitutions under immune pressure cause antigenic drift, necessitating frequent updates to vaccine strains. While hemagglutination inhibition (HI) assays remain the gold standard for assessing antigenic relationships, their labor-intensive and low-throughput nature limits scalability. Fortunately, the rapid accumulation of HA1 sequences enables sequence-based antigenic prediction, yet effectively extracting informative representations from these viral
papers.summary: VirPLM fine-tunes a protein language model to predict antigenic relationships between influenza A/H3N2 strains directly from hemagglutinin HA1 sequences, offering a scalable alternative to labor-intensive hemagglutination inhibition assays. By learning informative representations from the rapidly growing pool of HA1 sequences, the method aims to support more timely vaccine strain selection.

papers.title: Regulatory-prior-guided attention preserves biological structure during unpaired single-cell RNA-ATAC integration.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing and single-cell ATAC sequencing provide complementary views of transcriptional output and chromatin regulatory potential, but integrating unpaired profiles remains challenging because the modalities differ in feature space, sparsity and noise. Existing approaches often frame integration as distribution matching, which can over-align biologically distinct, condition-specific or modality-specific cell states. We present scHPGT, a single-cell Heterogeneous Prior-Guided Transformer for regulatory-prior-guided integration of unpaired RNA and chromatin accessibility profil
papers.summary: The authors present scHPGT, a transformer-based method that integrates unpaired single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq data by incorporating regulatory priors (e.g., gene-peak relationships) to guide alignment. This prior-guided attention mechanism helps preserve biologically meaningful structure, avoiding the over-alignment of distinct cell states that plagues distribution-matching approaches. The method addresses a key challenge in single-cell multi-omics integration when paired measurements are unavailable.

papers.title: Beyond the drug-centric view: Advancing AI virtual cell platforms for environmental perturbation modelling.
papers.abstract: Environmental exposures contribute substantially to global morbidity and mortality, with their biological effects shaped by factors such as dose, exposure duration, life-stage timing, and cumulative or sequential exposure patterns. With rapid advances in AI based virtual cell (VC) technologies, current frameworks emphasize genet-ic and pharmacological perturbations, leaving environmental perturbations insufficiently modelled. This imbal-ance is due to fundamental structural limitations in data availability, chemical space coverage, and representa-tional design, as well as lacking standardized
papers.summary: This perspective argues that current AI virtual cell platforms are heavily focused on genetic and pharmacological perturbations, leaving environmental exposures—such as pollutants and chemicals—poorly modelled. The authors attribute this gap to structural limitations in data availability, chemical space coverage, and representation design, and call for advancing VC frameworks to better capture dose, timing, and cumulative exposure effects.

papers.title: Training a force field for proteins and small molecules from scratch.
papers.abstract: Force fields for molecular dynamics are usually developed manually, limiting their transferability and making systematic exploration of functional forms challenging. We developed a graph neural network that assigns all force field parameters for diverse molecules using continuous atom typing. The freely-available model, called Garnet, was trained on quantum mechanical, condensed phase and protein nuclear magnetic resonance data without the use of existing parameters. The resulting force field shows comparable performance to current force fields on small molecules, folded proteins, protein comp
papers.summary: The authors developed Garnet, a graph neural network that assigns all force field parameters for both proteins and small molecules using continuous atom typing, trained from scratch on quantum mechanical, condensed phase, and protein NMR data without any existing parameters. The resulting force field performs comparably to current force fields on small molecules, folded proteins, and protein complexes, demonstrating that data-driven force field development is feasible.

papers.title: An open benchmark and language models for AI in aging biology.
papers.abstract: Over the past two decades, human aging has been characterized across DNA methylation, transcriptomic, proteomic, and clinical modalities, yet no benchmark evaluates whether AI systems can interpret these heterogeneous data types in the context of aging biology. We introduce LongevityBench, an open suite of 17 tasks spanning five biodata domains, and use it to assess 18 frontier AI systems from six developer teams. Despite recent advances in AI, no single model dominates all tasks, with omics-based age prediction being the hardest task regardless of scale. To test whether these gaps can be clos
papers.summary: The authors introduce LongevityBench, an open benchmark of 17 tasks across five biodata domains designed to evaluate how well AI systems can interpret aging-related data. Testing 18 frontier AI models, they find that no single model excels across all tasks, and omics-based age prediction remains the hardest challenge regardless of model scale. The work also explores whether these gaps can be closed with specialized language models.

papers.title: Machine learning-driven decoding of maternal immune signatures in repeated pregnancy loss.
papers.abstract: Repeated pregnancy loss (RPL) is a multifactorial condition in which the underlying immunological mechanisms, particularly the disruption of maternal-fetal tolerance, remain incompletely understood. Although immune tolerance is critical for pregnancy success, the specific immune dysregulations contributing to RPL, particularly in euploid pregnancies, have been difficult to characterize. To address this, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing of decidual tissues from RPL patients and first-trimester controls. Our analysis initially revealed elevated expression of a transcriptional module of im
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell RNA sequencing of decidual tissue from patients with repeated pregnancy loss (RPL) and first-trimester controls, combined with machine learning, to identify maternal immune signatures associated with the condition. The analysis reveals elevated expression of a transcriptional module in immune cells, offering new insights into the immunological dysregulation underlying RPL in euploid pregnancies.

papers.title: MAPA: A Semantic Network Framework for Functional Module Discovery and Interpretation in Multi-Omics Data.
papers.abstract: Multi-omics technologies generate high-dimensional molecular signatures that provide unprecedented opportunities to uncover biological mechanisms. However, translating complex molecular alterations into coherent and interpretable functional insights remains a major challenge. Existing module discovery methods can identify groups of related features, but often lack direct biological interpretability, whereas pathway-based approaches frequently yield redundant results that complicate interpretation. Here, we present MAPA (Modular Analysis and Phenotype-informed Annotation using large language mo
papers.summary: MAPA is a semantic network framework that integrates multi-omics data with large language models to discover and interpret functional modules. It addresses the interpretability gap in existing module discovery methods by providing phenotype-informed biological annotations, while avoiding the redundancy common in pathway-based approaches. The tool aims to translate complex molecular alterations into coherent functional insights.

papers.title: Genolator enables protein function interpretation using a multimodal large language model fusing genomic and structural interpretation with natural language interaction.
papers.abstract: Decoding the genetic code to unveil its genome functionality is a monumental task which would greatly advance the understanding of disease mechanisms and development of targeted treatments. Although large language models (LLMs) have transformed natural language processing across diverse domains, translating the complex language of DNA into human-readable form remains challenging due to genomic data complexity and unexplored regions of the human genome. Current language models either are capable of processing natural language or the genomic code. Models fusing both aspects are largely lacking.
papers.summary: Genolator is a multimodal large language model that integrates genomic sequence data with protein structural information and natural language interaction to interpret protein function. It addresses the gap in existing models that handle either natural language or genomic code but not both, aiming to make DNA-to-function translation more accessible and informative.

papers.title: TRPM8 virtual screening: the essential role of target-specific, inactive-enriched machine-learning scoring functions.
papers.abstract: The Transient Receptor Potential Melastatin 8 (TRPM8) ion channel is an emerging therapeutic target implicated in pain, inflammation and other disorders. While structure-based virtual screening (VS) is widely used in drug discovery, the effectiveness of generic and target-specific machine-learning (ML) scoring functions (SFs) for ion channels such as TRPM8 remains to be investigated. We established the first comprehensive structure-based VS benchmark for TRPM8. This evaluates classical docking SFs, generic ML SFs and target-specific ML models retrospectively across multiple TRPM8 protein confo
papers.summary: This study establishes the first comprehensive structure-based virtual screening benchmark for the TRPM8 ion channel, a therapeutic target for pain and inflammation. It compares classical docking scoring functions, generic machine-learning scoring functions, and target-specific ML models across multiple TRPM8 protein conformations. The key finding is that target-specific, inactive-enriched ML scoring functions substantially improve virtual screening performance for this challenging ion channel target.

papers.title: BAN-SDBPred: Improving Single-Stranded and Double-Stranded DNA-Binding Protein Prediction Using an Attention Network with Bilinear Convolution and Adaptive Sampling Strategy.
papers.abstract: DNA binding proteins play essential roles in numerous biological mechanisms. The DBPs can be either single-stranded binding (SSBs) or double-stranded binding (DSBs) to a DNA molecule. The in-depth identification of SSBs and DSBs has been a hot topic in bioinformatics and is involved in the drug discovery process. Traditional experimental methods failed to characterize the types of DBPs because of high cost and time constraints. While computational prediction of novel SSBs and DSBs has made significant progress, there are still challenges remaining in enhancing overall prediction performance. M
papers.summary: BAN-SDBPred is a computational tool that predicts whether a DNA-binding protein interacts with single-stranded or double-stranded DNA. It combines an attention network with bilinear convolution and an adaptive sampling strategy to improve prediction accuracy over existing methods. The approach aims to support drug discovery and functional annotation of DNA-binding proteins without costly experiments.

papers.title: Sequence optimization targeting mRNA stability enhances monoclonal antibody titers in CHO cells.
papers.abstract: This study presents a DNA sequence optimization approach that integrates mRNA stability as a tunable design parameter to enhance monoclonal antibody expression in Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells. A comprehensive combinatorial library of synonymous coding-sequence variants of an IgG1 light chain was integrated as single copies at a defined genomic locus in CHO cells with identical regulatory elements. Steady-state mRNA abundance, quantified by deep sequencing of gDNA and mRNA, served as a proxy for mRNA stability. These data were used to train a machine learning model that predicts mRNA abund
papers.summary: This study shows that synonymous codon choices affecting mRNA stability can be rationally optimized to boost monoclonal antibody production in CHO cells. By integrating a combinatorial library of light-chain variants at a fixed genomic locus and using deep sequencing to measure mRNA abundance, the authors trained a machine learning model that predicts stability and guides sequence design, yielding higher antibody titers.

papers.title: Engineered Transformer Base Editor with Enhanced Editing Efficiency.
papers.abstract: Canonical cytosine base editors (CBEs) achieve precise C-to-T conversions without inducing DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs), yet their clinical potential remains hampered by substantial off-target (OT) mutations. The recently developed transformer base editor (tBE) significantly reduces both genomic and transcriptomic OT mutations by using a cleavable deoxycytidine deaminase inhibitor (dCDI) domain. However, the modest base editing efficiency limits its broader applications. Here, through rational deaminase engineering and fusion of a uracil DNA glycosylase inhibitor (UGI) domain, we developed
papers.summary: The authors engineered an improved transformer base editor (tBE) by rationally modifying the deaminase and adding a uracil DNA glycosylase inhibitor (UGI) domain, aiming to boost editing efficiency while retaining the low off-target profile of the original tBE. This addresses a key limitation of the tBE system, whose modest base editing efficiency has restricted its broader use.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Rheumatology and Systemic Inflammatory Diseases: From Pattern Recognition to Signal Analysis and Clinical Decision Support.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are transforming the landscape of rheumatological and systemic inflammatory disease management, offering unprecedented capacity to integrate complex, multidimensional data for diagnostic support, disease monitoring, and therapeutic decision-making. This comprehensive narrative review, based on a non-systematic literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar combined with the authors' clinical expertise, provides a clinically oriented synthesis of current and emerging AI applications across the full spectrum of immune-mediated inflam
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes current and emerging applications of AI and machine learning in rheumatology and systemic inflammatory diseases, covering diagnostic support, disease monitoring, and therapeutic decision-making. It highlights how these methods integrate complex, multidimensional clinical data to aid pattern recognition and signal analysis in immune-mediated conditions. The paper is clinically oriented and based on a non-systematic literature search combined with expert opinion.

papers.title: Biological Foundation Models for Complex Disease Research and Clinical Translation.
papers.abstract: Complex diseases, including cancer, rare genetic disorders, neurodevelopmental and psychiatric conditions, and neurodegenerative diseases, arise from interactions among genetic variation, gene regulation, and cellular states that are difficult to capture using a single data type or biological scale. Biological foundation models address this challenge by treating nucleotides and genes as tokens and learning representations that can be transferred to downstream biomedical and clinical tasks. In this review, we examine two major model classes, genomic sequence foundation models and cell foundatio
papers.summary: This review surveys biological foundation models, focusing on genomic sequence models and cell foundation models that treat nucleotides and genes as tokens to learn transferable representations. It argues these models can integrate genetic variation, gene regulation, and cellular states to address complex diseases like cancer and neurodegeneration. The paper discusses how such models may support clinical translation.

papers.title: The Evolution of Artificial Intelligence in Antibody Design: From Structure-Based Engineering to Generative Models.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed computational antibody engineering by enabling accurate prediction of antibody structures, rational optimization of therapeutic properties, and de novo antibody design. Recent advances in deep learning, protein language models, and generative AI have fundamentally changed the way antibodies are discovered and engineered. This review aims to present the historical evolution of computational antibody engineering, from early structure-based design strategies to modern AI-driven approaches, while highlighting the major computation
papers.summary: This review traces the evolution of computational antibody engineering from early structure-based design to modern AI-driven approaches, including deep learning, protein language models, and generative AI. It highlights how these advances enable accurate antibody structure prediction, rational optimization of therapeutic properties, and de novo antibody design.

papers.title: Shared pathogenic genes and therapeutic targets in periodontitis and systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis: An integrative bioinformatics and machine learning study.
papers.abstract: Periodontitis (PD) and systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis (sJIA) are chronic inflammatory diseases with potential clinical links, yet their shared molecular mechanisms remain unclear-patients with JIA face elevated periodontal risk, the temporomandibular joint affected in JIA shares inflammatory pathways with PD, Th17 cells drive both conditions, and glucocorticoid therapy may exacerbate periodontal vulnerability. This study aimed to explore the shared mechanisms and potential therapeutic targets of PD and sJIA using genetic expression data from the GEO database and performed comprehensive
papers.summary: This study integrates gene expression datasets from periodontitis and systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis to identify shared molecular mechanisms and potential therapeutic targets. Using bioinformatics and machine learning approaches, the authors pinpoint common pathogenic genes linking these two inflammatory conditions, which may explain their clinical association. The findings suggest candidate drug targets that could address both diseases simultaneously.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence and biomarker-driven prediction of post-coronary artery bypass grafting atrial fibrillation: Integrating clinical, genomic, and metabolic insights.
papers.abstract: Postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) remains one of the most frequent and consequential complications after coronary artery bypass grafting, occurring in 15%-30% of patients and contributing to increased morbidity, prolonged hospitalization, and higher long-term mortality. Despite decades of investigation, traditional risk models have shown limited predictive accuracy owing to the multifactorial nature of POAF.
papers.summary: This paper develops an AI-driven prediction model for postoperative atrial fibrillation after coronary artery bypass grafting by integrating clinical, genomic, and metabolic data. It aims to improve on traditional risk models, which have shown limited accuracy given the multifactorial nature of POAF, a complication affecting 15%-30% of patients.

papers.title: Integrating Plant-Based Coagulation and Explainable Machine Learning for Sustainable River Water Treatment.
papers.abstract: Industrial wastewater discharge has severely degraded freshwater resources, necessitating the development of sustainable and environmentally benign treatment technologies. This study investigates the performance of three plant-based natural coagulants, namely, Moringa leaf powder (MLP), banana peel powder (BPP), and neem leaf powder (NLP), for the treatment of Sirsa River water contaminated with organic pollutants and heavy metals. Coagulation-flocculation experiments were conducted under optimized operating conditions, and treatment efficiency was evaluated based on turbidity, chemical oxygen
papers.journal: Water environment research : a research publication of the Water Environment Federation
papers.summary: This study evaluates three plant-based natural coagulants (Moringa leaf, banana peel, and neem leaf powders) for treating contaminated river water, optimizing coagulation-flocculation conditions to reduce turbidity and pollutants. The authors integrate explainable machine learning to interpret and predict treatment performance, supporting sustainable water remediation approaches.

papers.title: FatPlants 2.0: an AI-powered platform integrating plant lipid genes, pathways, and literature.
papers.abstract: Plant lipid research depends on accessible databases that connect genes, pathways, and prior literature. However, currently available resources are fragmented, species-limited, and lack AI-powered interfaces for integrated querying. FatPlants 2.0 addresses these issues by integrating ARALIP, PlantFADB, and new Cuphea/Pennycress experimental data into a unified platform with 14 000 genes/proteins, 110 pathways across 5 species, and 57 000+ curated publications. The platform features LipidBot, an AI agent enabling natural language queries via graph-based pathway search and retrieval-augmented ge
papers.journal: The Plant journal : for cell and molecular biology
papers.summary: FatPlants 2.0 is a unified plant lipid database that integrates ARALIP, PlantFADB, and new Cuphea/Pennycress experimental data, covering 14,000 genes/proteins, 110 pathways across 5 species, and over 57,000 curated publications. It introduces LipidBot, an AI agent that allows natural language querying through graph-based pathway search and retrieval-augmented generation. The platform addresses fragmentation and species limitations in existing plant lipid resources.

papers.title: PhoSARte: identification of SARS-CoV-2 phosphorylation sites using contrastive learning and protein language models.
papers.abstract: Phosphorylation, a critical post-translational modification, is extensively altered during viral infections, including SARS-CoV-2, where it plays a central role in modulating host-pathogen interactions. Accurately identifying these specific phosphorylation sites is crucial for understanding viral pathogenesis, prioritizing antiviral targets, guiding therapeutic strategies, and strengthening preparedness for future viral outbreaks. Although several computational tools have been proposed to complement experimental phosphoproteomics, existing methods often show limited robustness, cross-viral gen
papers.summary: PhoSARte is a computational tool that uses contrastive learning combined with protein language models to predict phosphorylation sites specifically in SARS-CoV-2 proteins. It aims to improve on existing phosphoproteomics prediction methods, which often lack robustness and transferability across viral genomes. The tool is intended to help prioritize antiviral targets and understand host-pathogen interactions during infection.

papers.title: Structure-based virulence factor classification using a dual-driven graph transformer with a pretrained language model.
papers.abstract: Bacterial pathogenicity relies on a multitude of virulence factors (VFs). Identifying these factors is crucial for comprehending the molecular mechanisms driving bacterial pathogenesis and pinpointing potential targets for antivirulence strategies. While the identification of VFs has received extensive attention, there is still a lack of prediction from the perspective of VF classes. Moreover, most computational methods focus solely on sequence information for virulence proteins, neglecting spatial structure information. Here, a novel Structure-based Dual-driven Graph Transformer framework nam
papers.summary: The paper introduces a dual-driven graph transformer framework that combines protein language model embeddings with structural information to classify bacterial virulence factors into specific functional classes. This addresses a gap in existing computational methods, which typically predict virulence factors as a binary property and rely only on sequence data, ignoring spatial structure. The approach aims to improve the identification of virulence factor classes, which could aid in understanding bacterial pathogenesis and developing antivirulence strategies.

papers.title: KGTC-DDA:Drug-disease association prediction based on parallel graph isomorphism and transformer networks with cross-attention.
papers.abstract: Drug development is a complex, time-consuming, and costly process, making drug repurposing an important strategy for identifying new therapeutic applications for existing drugs. Computational drug-disease association (DDA) prediction has therefore attracted increasing attention in recent years. Although many existing methods incorporate similarity information and graph neural networks for DDA prediction, effectively capturing both local structural patterns and global dependencies, as well as modeling complex interactions between drugs and diseases, remains challenging. To address these limitat
papers.summary: The paper introduces KGTC-DDA, a computational model that combines parallel graph isomorphism networks with transformer networks and cross-attention to predict drug-disease associations for drug repurposing. It aims to capture both local structural patterns and global dependencies in drug-disease interaction graphs, addressing limitations of prior similarity- and GNN-based methods.

papers.title: DLRNA-BERTa: a transformer approach for predicting molecule-RNA binding affinities.
papers.abstract: Therapies targeting RNA are rapidly expanding, with 24 FDA-approved RNA therapeutics and over 130 currently in clinical trials, highlighting RNA's growing role in drug discovery. In this context, transformer-based language models provide a scalable and cost-effective approach to accelerate RNA-targeted drug discovery by enabling the prediction of molecule-RNA binding affinities directly from sequence information. This study introduces DLRNA-BERTa, a RoBERTa-based framework that integrates RNA-BERTa and ChemBERTa-v2 to model molecule-RNA binding affinities. The framework includes six RNA class-
papers.summary: DLRNA-BERTa is a RoBERTa-based framework that combines RNA-BERTa and ChemBERTa-v2 language models to predict binding affinities between small molecules and RNA directly from sequence information. This approach aims to accelerate RNA-targeted drug discovery by providing a scalable, cost-effective alternative to experimental binding assays.

papers.title: PMPIHGLL: predicting metabolite-protein interactions using dual hypergraph convolutional networks and large language models.
papers.abstract: Metabolite-protein interactions (MPIs) play pivotal roles in regulating cellular processes and metabolic pathways and have important implications for systems biology and drug discovery. Although several computational models have been proposed, alternative approaches are needed to broaden the methodological toolkit for MPI prediction. In this study, we developed a new deep-learning model for predicting MPIs. Chemical and protein large language models were used to generate informative representations of metabolites and proteins. For each entity type, we constructed two K-nearest-neighbor hypergr
papers.summary: This paper introduces PMPIHGLL, a deep-learning model that predicts interactions between metabolites and proteins by combining chemical and protein large language models with dual hypergraph convolutional networks. The approach generates informative representations of metabolites and proteins and models higher-order relationships via K-nearest-neighbor hypergraphs. It aims to broaden the computational toolkit for metabolite-protein interaction prediction, with implications for systems biology and drug discovery.

papers.title: ELISA (Embedding-Linked Interactive Single-cell Agent): an interpretable hybrid generative Artificial Intelligence agent for expression-grounded discovery in single-cell genomics.
papers.abstract: Translating single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data into mechanistic biological hypotheses remains a critical bottleneck, as agentic AI systems lack direct access to transcriptomic representations while expression foundation models remain opaque to natural language. Here, we introduce ELISA (Embedding-Linked Interactive Single-cell Agent), an interpretable framework that unifies single-cell generative pretrained transformer expression embeddings with biomedical bidirectional encoder representations from transformers-based semantic retrieval and large-language model (LLM)-mediated interpret
papers.summary: ELISA is a hybrid AI framework that combines single-cell expression embeddings from a generative pretrained transformer with biomedical text retrieval and LLM-mediated interpretation, enabling natural-language interaction with scRNA-seq data. This allows researchers to query transcriptomic representations directly and generate mechanistic hypotheses grounded in expression data, addressing the gap between opaque foundation models and agentic AI systems.

papers.title: From pixels to conservation: Deep learning for automated monitoring of rare and endangered wildlife.
papers.abstract: Conservation of rare and endangered species requires scalable monitoring solutions to address accelerating biodiversity loss. Deep learning has transformed wildlife monitoring, enabling automated species identification, individual tracking, demographic inference, and behavioral analysis from camera traps, drones, and video surveillance. This review systematically analyzes 159 wildlife monitoring studies (2014-2026) across four technical domains: species recognition, individual re-identification, soft biometrics (age/sex estimation), and behavior/pose analysis. We examine architectural evolutio
papers.summary: This review systematically analyzes 159 deep learning studies (2014-2026) for automated wildlife monitoring, covering species recognition, individual re-identification, soft biometrics, and behavior/pose analysis from camera traps, drones, and video. It synthesizes architectural trends and highlights how these tools can support scalable conservation of rare and endangered species.

papers.title: Impact of MRI modality selection on glioma sub-region segmentation using 3D U-Net and Attention U-Net: A comparative evaluation across ten MRI sequences.
papers.abstract: Accurate segmentation of glioma sub-regions is essential for treatment planning and clinical decision-making. The selection of MRI input modality plays a critical role in the performance of deep learning-based segmentation models, as each weighting captures distinct tissue contrasts and physiological characteristics. This study performed a comparative evaluation of the impact of MRI modality selection on semantic segmentation of glioma sub-regions.
papers.summary: This study systematically compared how different MRI sequence selections affect the accuracy of deep learning models (3D U-Net and Attention U-Net) in segmenting glioma sub-regions across ten MRI modalities. The findings highlight that the choice of input MRI weighting substantially influences segmentation performance, offering practical guidance for optimizing imaging protocols in neuro-oncology deep learning pipelines.

papers.title: Integrated renal histopathology, RNA decay, and protein degradation signatures enhance post-mortem interval prediction using machine-learning models in a veterinary forensic rat model.
papers.abstract: Accurate estimation of post-mortem interval (PMI) is essential in veterinary forensics for reconstructing events surrounding death and supporting legal, welfare, and biosecurity investigations. Traditional methods relying on gross and histological changes are often subjective and highly influenced by environmental factors. This study aimed to develop a multimodal molecular approach by integrating renal histopathological autolysis scoring, RNA decay profiles, and protein degradation kinetics, then comparing classical regression with machine-learning models for PMI prediction in a controlled rat
papers.summary: This study combines kidney histopathology, RNA decay, and protein degradation data to predict post-mortem interval in a controlled rat model, comparing classical regression with machine-learning approaches. The multimodal molecular integration improved PMI estimation over traditional subjective methods, though the work is limited to a veterinary forensic rat model.

papers.title: PMAVP: A Mamba-Inspired Deep Learning Framework for Antiviral Peptide Identification and Functional Activity Prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate computational prediction of antiviral peptides (AVPs) can accelerate peptide screening and reduce experimental costs. However, existing deep learning-based methods still suffer from severe class imbalance, over-reliance on handcrafted features and limited interpretability. Here, we propose PMAVP, a multi-task learning framework that integrates the ProtT5 pre-trained protein language model with a Mamba-inspired module for AVP identification and functional activity prediction. We use ProtT5 to extract deep semantic representations from peptide sequences and a Mamba module to capture lon
papers.summary: PMAVP is a multi-task deep learning framework that combines the ProtT5 protein language model with a Mamba-inspired sequence module to identify antiviral peptides and predict their functional activity. It aims to overcome class imbalance, reliance on handcrafted features, and limited interpretability in prior methods. The approach offers a computational tool to speed up antiviral peptide screening and reduce experimental costs.

papers.title: Deep Learning for Deciphering the Plant Cis-Regulatory Code.
papers.abstract: Much of the regulatory information that shapes plant gene expression lies outside protein-coding regions, including many loci associated with agronomic traits. Deep learning models use DNA sequences and multi-omics data to examine components of this cis-regulatory information. This review compares convolutional, Transformer-based and graph architectures used to represent local sequence features, chromatin state and three-dimensional genome organisation. We assess their applications to transcription-factor binding, chromatin accessibility, gene expression, non-coding variant prioritisation and
papers.summary: This review surveys deep learning architectures—convolutional, Transformer-based, and graph neural networks—used to decode plant cis-regulatory information from DNA sequence and multi-omics data. It compares how these models represent local sequence features, chromatin state, and 3D genome organization, and assesses their applications to transcription-factor binding, chromatin accessibility, gene expression prediction, and non-coding variant prioritization. The paper provides a structured overview of computational approaches for linking non-coding regulatory variation to agronomic traits in plants.

papers.title: scGPA: an LLM-assisted workflow for directional virtual gene perturbation analysis from single-cell transcriptomes.
papers.abstract: Existing virtual perturbation methods can often infer directional changes by comparing predicted post-perturbation expression profiles with control cells. However, workflows that directly return direction-specific downstream candidate genes together with confidence scores, evidence support and interpretable summaries remain limited. We developed scGPA, an LLM-assisted workflow system for directional single-cell virtual gene perturbation analysis.
papers.summary: scGPA is an LLM-assisted workflow that performs directional virtual gene perturbation analysis on single-cell transcriptomes, returning direction-specific downstream candidate genes along with confidence scores, supporting evidence, and interpretable summaries. It addresses the gap left by existing methods that can infer directional changes but rarely provide integrated, interpretable outputs for downstream gene candidates.

papers.title: A New Unsupervised Machine Learning Method for Metabarcoding Analysis Based on Selected Mock Community Data.
papers.abstract: DNA metabarcoding analysis has emerged as a powerful tool for biological monitoring, enabling the identification and assessment of biodiversity across ecosystems. Conventional analytical methods, including operational taxonomic unit (OTU) clustering and amplicon sequence variant (ASV) analysis, have demonstrated strengths and limitations, including bias in estimating biodiversity and challenges in detecting rare sequences. To address these challenges, we developed unsupervised machine learning (UML)-based methods utilizing hierarchical density-based spatial clustering of applications with nois
papers.summary: This paper introduces a new unsupervised machine learning approach for DNA metabarcoding analysis, using hierarchical density-based clustering (HDBSCAN) calibrated with mock community data. The method aims to overcome limitations of conventional OTU clustering and ASV approaches, such as biodiversity estimation bias and difficulty detecting rare sequences. It offers a data-driven alternative for identifying taxa in environmental DNA samples.

papers.title: Architectural good practices for reproducible benchmarking in protein machine learning.
papers.abstract: Reliable benchmarking in protein machine learning requires biological tasks, datasets, representations, execution conditions, and evaluation regimes to be explicitly defined and traceable. Protein-specific dependencies, including label semantics, negative-class construction, evolutionary relationships, similarity control, inferred structures, protein language model configurations, and potential pretraining contamination, can alter benchmark interpretation. This Perspective provides an operational, protein-specific synthesis of established reproducibility practices through an artefact-linked ar
papers.summary: This perspective article outlines architectural best practices for making benchmarking in protein machine learning reproducible and interpretable. It highlights protein-specific pitfalls such as label semantics, negative-class construction, evolutionary relationships, similarity control, inferred structures, protein language model configurations, and pretraining contamination that can distort benchmark results. The authors provide an operational, artefact-linked framework to help researchers design and report benchmarks more rigorously.

papers.title: RA-PLA: Retrieval-augmented graph convolutional networks for protein-ligand binding affinity prediction.
papers.abstract: Protein-ligand binding affinity (PLA) prediction is essential for computational drug discovery, yet existing deep learning methods typically employ a single globally trained model that fails to adapt to individual query samples. In this paper, we propose a novel end-to-end framework that retrieves hard protein-ligand pairs-samples whose nearest neighbors have conflicting labels under manifold smoothness constraints-and integrates them via a semi-supervised graph convolutional network (GCN). For each query, we automatically construct a graph where nodes represent protein-ligand pairs and edges
papers.summary: The authors introduce RA-PLA, a retrieval-augmented framework that improves protein-ligand binding affinity prediction by identifying 'hard' training pairs whose nearest neighbors have conflicting labels and incorporating them through a semi-supervised graph convolutional network. This allows the model to adapt to individual query samples rather than relying on a single globally trained model, potentially improving accuracy in computational drug discovery.

papers.title: Integrative Transcriptomic and Machine Learning Analysis Identifies JAG1 and NR2F2 in Keloid.
papers.abstract: To identify key genes associated with keloid through integrative analysis of multiple transcriptomic datasets, and to explore their potential regulatory roles in disease development with experimental validation.
papers.summary: This study integrates multiple transcriptomic datasets with machine learning to identify JAG1 and NR2F2 as key genes associated with keloid formation. The authors provide experimental validation supporting potential regulatory roles for these genes in keloid development.

papers.title: Machine learning models in predicting antimicrobial resistance in gonorrhea: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: The global rise in antimicrobial resistance (AMR) among Neisseria gonorrhoeae presents a major public health threat, complicating treatment and control efforts. Traditional diagnostic methods for AMR detection are time-consuming and often limited by laboratory resources, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. The rapid evolution of machine learning (ML) models offers new opportunities for predictive diagnostics that can enhance surveillance, optimize antibiotic therapy, and reduce transmission.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates machine learning models for predicting antimicrobial resistance in Neisseria gonorrhoeae, addressing a major public health threat where traditional diagnostics are slow and resource-intensive. The authors synthesize evidence on model performance, highlighting the potential of ML to improve surveillance, guide antibiotic therapy, and reduce transmission, especially in low- and middle-income settings.

papers.title: Shall we repeat? Predicting the necessity to repeat blood testing in pediatric emergency departments of laboratory tests previously performed in the community using a machine learning model.
papers.abstract: Community‑ordered laboratory blood tests are frequently re-ordered when the patients arrive at the pediatric emergency departments. When only a few hours separate the initial community blood tests from assessment in the emergency department, repeated laboratory testing often does not contribute to clinical management. Additional testing can inconvenience patients, increase out-of-pocket costs for patients and families, add costs to the healthcare system, and delay clinical decision-making. To address this issue, we collected community-issued laboratory tests for complete blood count, electroly
papers.summary: This study developed a machine learning model to predict whether blood tests ordered in the community need to be repeated when pediatric patients arrive at the emergency department. The goal is to reduce unnecessary repeat testing, which causes patient discomfort, extra costs, and delays in care. The model uses previously performed complete blood count and electrolyte test results to make these predictions.

papers.title: A parallel convolution attention network for crop genomic prediction.
papers.abstract: Genome prediction is a breeding strategy that predicts crop phenotype through genomic markers. Traditional statistical models cannot accurately capture the complex relationships between genotypes and phenotypes, and deep neural networks have shown significant advantages in capturing nonlinear relationships. Deep learning methods in genome selection primarily utilize sequential convolutional kernels, which can lead to challenges such as gradient disappearance and computational inefficiency. In this study a novel crop genomic prediction method based on a parallel convolutional attention network
papers.summary: This paper introduces a parallel convolutional attention network for genomic prediction in crops, aiming to better capture nonlinear genotype-phenotype relationships than traditional statistical models and sequential convolutional deep learning approaches. The proposed architecture is designed to mitigate gradient vanishing and improve computational efficiency.

papers.title: Single-cell RNA-seq and machine learning identify HMGN2 as a lactylation-associated hub gene in heart failure.
papers.abstract: Heart failure (HF) is a diverse condition characterized by dysregulated lactate metabolism and histone lactylation, which may contribute to maladaptive cardiac remodeling. However, the cell type-specific mechanisms underlying these processes remain poorly understood. To address this gap, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data from human failing and non-failing control hearts and assessed lactylation activity across identified cell types using multiple gene set scoring methods. Uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP) analysis revealed that fibroblasts and smooth
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell RNA-seq data from human failing and non-failing hearts with machine learning to identify cell-type-specific lactylation activity, highlighting fibroblasts and smooth muscle cells. The authors pinpoint HMGN2 as a lactylation-associated hub gene in heart failure, suggesting a potential mechanistic link between lactate metabolism, histone lactylation, and maladaptive cardiac remodeling.

papers.title: Development and validation of a machine learning scoring system based on multi-dimensional metabolic signatures for invasive examination triage in intestinal diseases.
papers.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) often present with overlapping gastrointestinal symptoms despite distinct pathophysiological mechanisms. Colonoscopy remains the diagnostic gold standard but is invasive, costly and frequently overutilized. Single biomarkers have limited diagnostic value because they do not fully reflect the complex metabolic and inflammatory alterations underlying intestinal diseases. We aimed to develop and validate an interpretable machine learning-based scoring system integrating multidimensional metabolism-related biomarkers for invasive
papers.summary: This study developed a machine learning scoring system that combines multiple metabolism-related biomarkers to help triage patients with intestinal diseases (IBD vs. IBS) and reduce unnecessary invasive colonoscopies. The model was designed to be interpretable and validated for distinguishing between these overlapping conditions.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Based Prediction of Lower Extremity Deep Vein Thrombosis in Patients with Acute Exacerbation of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.
papers.abstract: Patients with acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) have an increased risk of lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) due to inflammation, immobility, and coagulation abnormalities. This study aimed to develop a machine learning model for predicting DVT risk in AECOPD patients and identify important predictors.
papers.summary: This study develops a machine learning model to predict the risk of lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in patients hospitalized with acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD), a group at elevated thrombotic risk. The authors also identify key clinical predictors contributing to DVT risk in this population. The work aims to support earlier risk stratification and preventive decision-making in AECOPD care.

papers.title: Artificial-intelligence- and multi-omics-guided predictive and drug repurposing framework construction for colorectal cancer: evidence from succinylation-neutrophil signatures.
papers.abstract: Succinylation-linked metabolic rewiring and neutrophil-driven inflammation are key drivers of colorectal carcinoma (COAD) progression; however, they have rarely been translated to an end-to-end artificial intelligence (AI) drug-design pipeline connecting target nomination, resistance-relevant tumor microenvironment states, and candidate evaluation.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This paper builds an AI- and multi-omics-driven framework for colorectal cancer that links succinylation-related metabolic rewiring and neutrophil-driven inflammation to drug repurposing candidates. The authors use these succinylation-neutrophil signatures to nominate targets, characterize resistance-relevant tumor microenvironment states, and evaluate candidate drugs in an end-to-end pipeline.

papers.title: Integrative transcriptomic analysis identifies CCL22-associated immune signatures in air pollution-related atopic dermatitis.
papers.abstract: Air pollution has been associated with the development and exacerbation of atopic dermatitis (AD), but the molecular signatures connecting pollutant-related targets with AD-associated immune dysregulation remain incompletely characterized.
papers.summary: This study integrates transcriptomic data to identify molecular signatures linking air pollution exposure to atopic dermatitis, highlighting CCL22-associated immune pathways. The findings suggest that pollutant-related targets may drive immune dysregulation in AD, offering potential biomarkers or therapeutic targets.

papers.title: A trainable language model with potential to modulate translation rates in non-model organisms by generating upstream untranslated region sequence libraries.
papers.abstract: Tuning protein expression in non-model organisms is often constrained by the lack of validated genetic parts and predictive design tools. Translational tuning through the modulation of upstream untranslated regions (5'-UTRs) offers a potentially organism-agnostic route, but existing methods typically rely on mechanistic assumptions, prior knowledge that may not be available in non-model contexts, or the screening of sequence libraries. Here, we present a simple generative approach for creating synthetic 5'-UTR libraries based solely on the genomic sequence statistics of any desired organism. T
papers.summary: The authors present a trainable language model that generates synthetic 5'-UTR sequence libraries using only the genomic sequence statistics of a target organism, without requiring prior mechanistic knowledge or validated genetic parts. This approach aims to enable translational tuning in non-model organisms by providing an organism-agnostic, data-driven route to modulate translation rates.

papers.title: Protein language model-generated enzyme sequences exhibit high stability in molecular dynamics simulations.
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have transformed protein engineering by capturing complex sequence patterns from large datasets, enabling applications such as structure prediction and functional annotation. Finenzyme applies conditional transfer learning to generate biologically plausible enzyme sequences conditioned on Enzyme Commission (EC) numbers.
papers.summary: This study evaluates enzyme sequences generated by Finenzyme, a conditional protein language model that produces sequences based on Enzyme Commission numbers, using molecular dynamics simulations. The generated sequences show high structural stability, suggesting that language model outputs can yield biologically plausible and stable enzymes.

papers.title: Multimodal molecular features enable interpretable umami peptide screening and structure-activity analysis.
papers.abstract: Umami peptides are important taste-active components in protein-rich foods, but their computational discovery is still constrained by predictors that rely mainly on sequence information and provide limited mechanistic interpretability. In this study, BioPP-GFD was developed as an interpretable multimodal deep learning framework for umami peptide screening and structure-activity analysis. The model integrates molecular graphs, molecular fingerprints, and physicochemical descriptors through adaptive channel attention. In the umami-bitter peptide classification task, BioPP-GFD achieved an accurac
papers.summary: This study presents BioPP-GFD, a multimodal deep learning framework that integrates molecular graphs, fingerprints, and physicochemical descriptors to screen for umami peptides and analyze their structure-activity relationships. The model outperforms sequence-only predictors and offers improved mechanistic interpretability for taste-active peptide discovery.

papers.title: BeitAI-pHLA: Multiallele Peptide-HLA Class I Binding Prediction Using Protein Language Model and Multi-Instance Learning.
papers.abstract: Human leukocyte antigen (HLA) molecules participate in cellular immune responses by binding to peptide fragments derived from antigens. Exploring this process is crucial to understanding the mechanisms and underlying factors that regulate the cellular immune system. Due to the extreme polymorphism of HLA, the peptides obtained from mass spectrometry of eluted ligand experiments typically correspond to multiple HLA alleles. They are thus poly-specific, providing various options for HLA assignments. This introduces notable challenges for accurate peptide-HLA assignment and interpretation. To add
papers.summary: BeitAI-pHLA is a computational method for predicting peptide-HLA class I binding that handles the common situation where mass spectrometry experiments yield peptides that could bind multiple HLA alleles. It combines a protein language model with multi-instance learning to assign peptides to their correct HLA alleles and predict binding across multiple alleles simultaneously. This addresses a key bottleneck in immunopeptidomics where poly-specific peptide data complicates accurate HLA assignment.

papers.title: Skill-File-Guided Virtual Screening: A Single-Target Formyl Peptide Receptor 2 Case Study of Large-Language-Model-Coordinated Physics and Diffusion Docking.
papers.abstract: Background: Virtual screening outcomes depend on protocol choices normally made implicitly by experts. I tested whether encoding that expertise as a "skill file" (a Markdown reference read by a large-language-model coding agent) changes virtual screening outcomes versus naive agent defaults, in a single-target case study on formyl peptide receptor 2 (FPR2; Protein Data Bank 7T6S, 3.0 Å cryo-electron microscopy). Methods: A Claude Code agent curated 1,000 pChEMBL ≥5 FPR2 actives and 9,829 property-matched decoys, prepared ligand libraries under naive and skill-guided protocols, and screened the
papers.summary: This case study tests whether encoding expert virtual-screening protocol choices into a Markdown 'skill file' that guides a large-language-model coding agent improves screening outcomes for the formyl peptide receptor 2 (FPR2) target. The agent curated 1,000 known FPR2 actives and 9,829 matched decoys and ran ligand library preparation under naive versus skill-guided protocols. The work illustrates how LLM-coordinated workflows can make expert methodological decisions explicit and reproducible in structure-based drug discovery.
